# Fragment Length and End-Motif Features

The two feature families of the [[fragmentomics-classifier|Fragmentomics Classifier]]. They describe how cell-free DNA is cut, not what sequence variants it carries, so they can detect tumour-derived DNA without knowing the tumour's mutations.

## Definition

> [!abstract]
> Fragment-length features describe how long the molecules are, genome-wide and per region; end-motif features describe which short sequences sit at the molecule ends. Tumour-derived cfDNA tends to be shorter and to have a shifted end-motif spectrum, but the two families respond very differently to pre-analytical variation.

## Fragment-Length Features

- **Length histogram**: proportion of fragments in 2 bp bins from 90 to 220 bp, normalised per sample (66 features).
- **Short-to-long ratios**: fragments of 100–150 bp over 151–220 bp in 5 Mb windows across the autosomes after GC correction (about 540 windows), following the DELFI-style approach.
- **Summary features**: modal length, fraction below 150 bp, and the 10 bp periodicity amplitude below 150 bp.

Tumour cfDNA is enriched for shorter fragments, and selecting fragments below 150 bp increases apparent tumour fraction; see [[jin-2021-hcc-fragment-size-end-motifs]]. This is the family with the most signal at low tumour fraction in St Aldric.

It is also the family most affected by extraction and library preparation. The kit lot change of 2025-06-16 shifted the modal length by about 3 bp and increased the sub-150 bp fraction ([[extraction-kit-lot-change-2025-06-16]], [[classifier-batch-effect-analysis-2026-03]]). GC bias interacts with length, so GC correction runs at fragment level before ratios are computed (approach after [[spiegl-2023-gcparagon]]).

## End-Motif Features

- **4-mer end-motif frequencies**: the 256 possible 4-mers at the 5' end of each read pair, normalised to sum to one.
- **Motif diversity score**: normalised Shannon entropy of the 256 frequencies.
- **Selected motif ratios**: a handful of motifs reported as cancer-associated in the literature, such as CCCA and CCTG ([[jin-2021-hcc-fragment-size-end-motifs]]), kept as interpretable summaries.

End motifs reflect nuclease activity and nucleosome position; [[ju-2024-cfdna-end-characteristics]] shows that ends located inside nucleosomes are shorter and carry altered motifs. Per sample they are noisier than length features at shallow depth, but in our data they moved very little across the extraction lots: leave-batch-out AUC of the end-motif model dropped by only 0.02.

## How the Classifier Uses Them

The asymmetry between the two families is the reason for the stacked design ([[classifier-design-review-2026-04-02]]): length features go into a regularised logistic regression after batch correction, where shrinkage limits how much batch-specific structure the model can absorb; end-motif features go into gradient boosting, which can capture motif interactions and did not overfit batches. A logistic meta-learner combines the two scores ([[model-stacking]]). Details and coefficients are in [[classifier-model-card-v2]]; ablations in [[classifier-feature-ablation-results]].

## Pitfalls

- Reference genome and alignment choices bias fragment features in sample-dependent ways ([[liu-2024-reference-biases-fragmentomics]]); keep the reference and aligner fixed across cohorts and record them in the model card.
- Feature definitions must be identical at every site for external validation; this is one reason we want Halo sites to run our container rather than their own feature code.
- In our hands, length profiles from enzymatic methylation panel reads were shifted relative to shallow WGS of the same extract, so features come from the shallow WGS libraries only, never from panel reads.
